mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through stronger corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The combined signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 240) triggers Federal Reserve tightening, which initially depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which is a leading indicator of positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to stronger corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1000 thousand units signals weakening residential construction, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 1000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) confirms a strong labor market, which drives consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined signal of falling UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a very tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement aggressive monetary tightening to curb wage inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0.
